name: Protected File Guard

# Server-side enforcement of the tier/squad model. The client-side
# .claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh is non-blocking — this workflow is the
# authoritative gate at PR time.

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - main
      - 'release/**'
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 1 — Warning (non-blocking): Tier 1 files touched.
  # NOT a required status check (see AGENTS.md > Tier 1 Approval for why).
  # The actual hard block is CODEOWNERS + require_code_owner_reviews on
  # branch protection, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
  # involvement. This job exists to post the loud, informative warning and
  # owner-contact-map — useful context, not the gate itself.
  #
  # History: this used to be a required check with a second job
  # (tier1-guard-recheck) that re-evaluated it on every review submission
  # via the Checks API, so it could flip from fail to pass without a new
  # commit. That approach stopped working once GitHub locked down check-run
  # updates to same-run-only in Feb 2025 (see
  # https://github.blog/changelog/2025-02-12-notice-of-upcoming-deprecations-and-breaking-changes-for-github-actions/#changes-to-check-run-status-modification) —
  # a different workflow run can no longer flip another run's check
  # conclusion. Since a single pull_request-triggered run can't wait around
  # for a future review, and re-running the whole job on review events just
  # creates a second, stale-vs-fresh check-run record under the same name
  # (which GitHub does NOT treat the newer one as superseding for
  # merge-blocking purposes), there's no way to make this job itself both
  # required and reliably self-updating. CODEOWNERS already does this
  # correctly and natively, so that's the real gate.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  tier1-guard:
    name: "🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      - name: Get changed files
        id: changed
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          base_sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          files_yaml: |
            tier1:
              # Design tokens — owner: UI Designer
              - 'overrides/app/theme/foundation/**'
              - 'overrides/app/theme/index.ts'
              # Commerce SDK hooks (overrides surface) — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.*'
              # Runtime & integration config — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'config/**'
              - 'overrides/app/ssr.*'
              - 'worker/main.*'
              - 'mobify.config.js'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'package-lock.json'
              # Test & tooling config — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'vitest.config.*'
              - 'playwright.config.*'
              - '.storybook/**'
              - 'tests/lighthouserc.*'
              - 'lighthouserc.*'
              # CI/CD — owner: Integration Lead
              - '.github/workflows/**'
              # Governance — owner: Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead
              - 'AGENTS.md'
              - 'CLAUDE.md'
              - 'CODEOWNERS'
              - '.claude/rules/**'
              - '.claude/settings.json'
              - 'coderabbit.yaml'
              - '.coderabbit/**'
              - 'semgrep.yml'
              - 'scripts/hooks/**'

      - name: Warn if Tier 1 files changed (informational — not a merge block)
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier1_any_changed == 'true'
        run: |
          echo ""
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo "🔴 TIER 1 PROTECTED FILES DETECTED IN THIS PR"
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo ""
          echo "The following frozen files have been modified:"
          echo ""
          echo "${{ steps.changed.outputs.tier1_all_changed_files }}" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/^/  ❌ /'
          echo ""
          echo "These files require an approving code-owner review before merge."
          echo "This check is informational — the actual merge block is CODEOWNERS +"
          echo "the required code-owner review, enforced by GitHub natively."
          echo ""
          echo "REQUIRED ACTIONS before this PR can be merged:"
          echo "  1. Get an approving review (not just a comment) from a member of"
          echo "     @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers — CODEOWNERS auto-requests this."
          echo "  2. Contact the correct owner using the table below"
          echo ""
          echo "OWNER CONTACT MAP:"
          echo "  overrides/app/theme/foundation/      → UI Designer      (#design-system)"
          echo "  overrides/app/theme/index.ts         → UI Designer      (#design-system)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-current-*   → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein    → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud   → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-tok → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  config/                             → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/ssr.*                 → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  worker/main.*                       → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  mobify.config.js                    → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  package.json (root)                 → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  vitest/playwright/.storybook config → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  .github/workflows/                  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / CODEOWNERS  → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  .claude/rules/ / .claude/settings   → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  coderabbit.yaml / .coderabbit/      → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  semgrep.yml / scripts/hooks/        → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo ""
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"

      - name: Pass — no Tier 1 files changed
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier1_any_changed == 'false'
        run: |
          echo "✅ No Tier 1 protected files detected in this PR."

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 2 — Hard block: PR targeting wrong branch
  # Prevents direct PRs to main that bypass develop
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  branch-target-guard:
    name: "🔴 Branch Target Check"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Block direct PRs to main from feature branches
        run: |
          BASE="${{ github.base_ref }}"
          HEAD="${{ github.head_ref }}"

          echo "Base branch: $BASE"
          echo "Head branch: $HEAD"

          # Feature branches must not go directly to main
          if [[ "$BASE" == "main" && "$HEAD" == feature/* ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            echo "🔴 INVALID BRANCH TARGET"
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            echo ""
            echo "Feature branches must target 'develop', not 'main'."
            echo ""
            echo "Correct flow: feature/* → develop → (release/*) → main"
            echo ""
            echo "Please update the base branch of this PR to 'develop'."
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "✅ Branch target is valid."

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 3 — Warning (non-blocking): Tier 2 files touched
  # Posts a PR comment listing Tier 2 files and required reviewers
  # Does NOT fail the build — but CodeRabbit will escalate review
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  tier2-warning:
    name: "🟡 Tier 2 — Protected Files Warning"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Get changed Tier 2 files
        id: changed
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          files_yaml: |
            tier2:
              # Global shell — both squads
              - 'overrides/app/components/header/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/footer/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/list-menu/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/seo/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/_app/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/_app-config/**'
              - 'overrides/app/routes.*'
              # Shared product components — Squad B primary, Squad A notified
              - 'overrides/app/components/product-tile/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/product-item/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/display-price/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/image-gallery/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/swatch-group/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/recommended-products/**'
              # Shared commerce components — Squad A primary, Squad B notified
              - 'overrides/app/components/order-summary/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/promo-code/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/**'
              # Theme component styles — UI Designer
              - 'overrides/app/theme/components/**'
              # Translations — Integration / SI Partner
              - 'translations/**'
              - 'overrides/app/static/translations/**'
              # Shared hooks — both squads
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-currency.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-dnt-notification.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-app-origin.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-selected-store.*'

      - name: Post Tier 2 warning comment on PR
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier2_any_changed == 'true'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const files = `${{ steps.changed.outputs.tier2_all_changed_files }}`
              .split(' ')
              .filter(Boolean)
              .map(f => `- \`${f}\``)
              .join('\n');

            const body = `## 🟡 Tier 2 Protected Files Detected

            This PR modifies shared components or hooks that are used across multiple features or squads.
            This is **not a merge block** — but it requires a second-developer review before merging.

            **Files affected:**
            ${files}

            **Required before merge:**
            - [ ] A developer from the **other squad** (not the PR author's squad) has reviewed and approved
            - [ ] The UI Designer has been notified if \`overrides/app/theme/components/\` is included
            - [ ] The Integration / SI Partner has been notified if \`translations/\` is included
            - [ ] No prop signature or export changes have been made without updating all consumers

            **Why this matters:** These files are imported by components in both Squad A and Squad B.
            A breaking change here — even a small one — will affect both squads simultaneously.

            _This comment is auto-generated by the Protected File Guard workflow._`;

            // Check if we already posted this comment to avoid duplicates
            const comments = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existing = comments.data.find(c =>
              c.body.includes('Tier 2 Protected Files Detected') &&
              c.user.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
            );

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

      - name: Pass — no Tier 2 files changed
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier2_any_changed == 'false'
        run: |
          echo "✅ No Tier 2 protected files detected in this PR."

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 4 — Cross-squad boundary detection
  # Warns when a PR touches both Squad A and Squad B territory
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cross-squad-guard:
    name: "🟡 Cross-Squad Boundary Check"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Detect Squad A files changed
        id: squad-a
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          files_yaml: |
            squad_a:
              - 'overrides/app/pages/cart/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/checkout/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/checkout-one-click/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/confirmation/**'

              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-checkout-auto-select.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-multiship.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-pickup-shipment.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-sf-payments.*'

      - name: Detect Squad B files changed
        id: squad-b
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          files_yaml: |
            squad_b:
              - 'overrides/app/pages/home/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/product-list/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/search/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/account/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/wishlist/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/store-locator/**'

              - 'overrides/app/components/store-locator/**'

              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-derived-product.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-variant.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-wish-list.*'

      - name: Warn on cross-squad PR
        if: |

content.content: 1 # Components, Hooks & Storybook 2 3 Everything about designing, structuring, and presenting a React component or hook in this 4 project. Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting 5 rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic 6 numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS 7 conventions live in [css.md](./css.md). 8 9 --- 10 11 ## Components 12 13 - **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`). 14 No default exports of anonymous functions. 15 - **Props type name** matches the component name: `ProductTileProps` for `ProductTile`, 16 `TopNavProps` for `TopNav`. 17 - **Props type placement:** 18 - _Default:_ declare the `Props` type at the top of the component file. 19 - _Move to `types.ts` in the same folder_ only when (a) the type is consumed by sibling 20 files (story, test, sub-components) **or** (b) it exceeds ~30 lines and mixes with 21 other shared types worth co-locating. 22 - The trigger is _shared consumption_, not line count alone. 23 - **JSDoc** is required on: 24 25 - Any component used by ≥2 callers (shared components — typically Tier 2 in 26 [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)). 27 - Any exported hook. 28 - Any utility function with non-obvious behaviour. 29 30 Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient. 31 32 - **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`). 33 - **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions 34 for "I forgot to mark it optional." 35 - **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get 36 these right at authoring time:** 37 - Every `` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images). 38 - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs 39 an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to 40 announce. 41 - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`, 42 `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role` 43 attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an 44 `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which 45 is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour). 46 47 --- 48 49 ## Composition — writing a "clean" component 50 51 Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline 52 state belongs in a custom hook instead. 53 54 - **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and 55 avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent 56 paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced** 57 — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so 58 treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not 59 something the build will fail on yet. If this keeps being a problem in practice, adding 60 those two ESLint rules is a cheap follow-up (they're built into ESLint core, no new 61 dependency needed). 62 - **Container/presentational separation.** Anything under `overrides/app/components/` 63 receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like 64 `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or any `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` 65 / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container 66 component, which then passes the result down. This generalizes the existing 67 "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just 68 commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own 69 data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, 70 mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it). 71 - **Extract-to-hook threshold.** Pull inline component logic out into a custom hook 72 (`overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`) when either is true: 73 74 - The component has ≥2 pieces of related `useState` that change together (a strong signal 75 the state belongs in one place, whether that's a custom hook or a single reducer). 76 - Any `useEffect` has a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function — non-trivial 77 meaning more than a single obvious dependency, or the effect does anything beyond a 78 one-line side effect. 79 80 This one is judgment-heavy, not a hard mechanical gate — `/code-quality` should flag it as 81 a should-fix, not a must-fix, and a component with ≥4 `useState` calls is a reasonable 82 coarse trigger to at least stop and ask "should this be a hook?" 83 84 --- 85 86 ## Hooks 87 88 - **File extension** is `.ts` (no JSX in a hook file). 89 - **Exported function name** matches the filename: `useWishlist.ts` exports `useWishlist`. 90 - **Parameters and return value are typed** — no implicit `any`, no missing return type. 91 See [typescript.md](./typescript.md) for the general typing rules this extends. 92 - **JSDoc** is required on every exported hook, including a `@returns` description. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## Storybook 97 98 Storybook is the canonical place to view components in isolation. Keep it browsable — 99 a flat 200-story sidebar is unusable. 100 101 ### When a story is required 102 103 - **Required** for any component exported from its folder under `overrides/app/components/` 104 or `overrides/app/pages/` (i.e. anything another file imports). 105 - **Not required** for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent 106 (e.g. `productTile/priceRow.tsx` used only by `productTile/index.tsx`). Cover their 107 variants via the parent's stories. 108 - Pages get a story showing the full assembly with representative props — not a story per 109 sub-section. 110 111 ### Categorisation 112 113 Story `title` drives the sidebar tree. Pick the first matching category: 114 115 | Category | What goes here | 116 | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 117 | `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons, Shadows | 118 | `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — both display (Badge, Tag, Link, Avatar, Skeleton) and interactive controls (Button, Input, Checkbox, Select). Tiebreaker: _can it be used outside a form?_ → `Elements/`. | 119 | `Layout/` | Global chrome, navigation, and structural components — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, ListMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination, Seo | 120 | `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared components — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup | 121 | `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, CheckoutContactForm, NewsletterSignup | 122 | `Pages/` | Full page assemblies — PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout, Account | 123 | `Contentful/` | CMS-driven components — HeroBanner, RichText, ContentBlock. Use mock Contentful data in stories so variants are visible without a live CMS connection. | 124 125 Naming convention: singular for a concept or proper noun (`Foundation`, `Commerce`, `Layout`, `Contentful`); plural for a collection (`Elements`, `Forms`, `Pages`). 126 127 Examples: 128 129 ```ts 130 export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅ 131 export default { title: 'Layout/Header' }; // ✅ 132 export default { title: 'Elements/Button' }; // ✅ 133 export default { title: 'Pages/PDP' }; // ✅ 134 export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ — eCommerce specific, use Commerce/ 135 export default { title: 'Primitives/Button' }; // ❌ — use Elements/ 136 ``` 137 138 When in doubt: ask "what does this component _know_ about?" Commerce → `Commerce/`, 139 CMS-driven → `Contentful/`, nothing domain-specific → `Elements/`, page-level composition → `Pages/`. 140 141 ### Story content 142 143 - Every story file has a `Default` named export. 144 - Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`) — not 145 for every possible prop combination. 146 - `play` functions only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting; otherwise the 147 story is purely visual. 148

# CSS & Styling Conventions

Chakra UI and `.scss` conventions. See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Rules > Styling for the
higher-level policy (Chakra props first, `.scss` only when insufficient, theme file
ownership/tiers) — this file covers the concrete day-to-day rules underneath that policy.

---

## Tokens — no hardcoded design values

Chakra UI props must use the Chakra token system — no hardcoded hex colours, no pixel
values for spacing, no raw font sizes. Tokens belong in
[overrides/app/theme/foundation/](../../overrides/app/theme/) (Tier 1 — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)).

```tsx
// ❌ hardcoded
<Box color="#1A1A1A" padding="16px" fontSize="14px" />

// ✅ token
<Box color="brand.primary" padding={4} fontSize="sm" />
```

**Not currently mechanically enforced.** Unlike the accessibility rules in
[components.md](./components.md), there's no `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` rule watching for
a raw hex code or `px` value landing in a Chakra prop or `.scss` file yet — this is a strong
candidate for the same treatment (ast-grep can pattern-match a hex-colour or `px` literal
inside a JSX attribute value) if hardcoded values keep slipping through review.

---

## `.scss` — only when Chakra props are insufficient

Per AGENTS.md, reach for a `.scss` file alongside a component only when Chakra's prop system
genuinely can't express what's needed (e.g. complex pseudo-selectors, keyframe animations,
print styles). When you do:

- **File naming:** matches the component file exactly — `productTile.scss` next to
  `productTile/index.tsx` (see [conventions.md](./conventions.md) > File naming and folder
  structure for the folder layout this sits in).
- **Scoped, co-located only.** No global stylesheets outside `overrides/app/theme/` — a
  component's `.scss` file must only affect that component's own markup.
- **Nesting depth ≤ 3 levels.** Beyond that, the selector is almost always reaching into a
  child component's internals rather than styling its own root — a sign the styling belongs
  in that child instead, or that Chakra's `sx` prop / a theme variant would express it more
  directly.
- **No ID selectors.** Class-based only — an ID selector's specificity makes it
  disproportionately hard to override later (including by a legitimate future Chakra
  variant), and IDs aren't guaranteed unique when a component renders more than once on a
  page.
- **No `!important`** without an inline comment explaining why the override is genuinely
  unavoidable (e.g. fighting a third-party widget's inline styles) — same reasoning as the
  `any`/non-null-assertion escape hatches in [typescript.md](./typescript.md): allowed, but
  the reason has to be visible at the point of use, not left for the next reader to guess.
- **Prefer Chakra's `sx` prop or a theme variant extension over a new `.scss` file** for
  anything that's really just "a Chakra style the prop system doesn't have a named prop for"
  — a new global class is a bigger footprint than a one-off `sx` override, and `sx` keeps the
  style co-located with the JSX that uses it instead of a separate file to keep in sync.

content.text: Here's the full picture of CodeRabbit in this repo — it spans three files, all Tier 1, plus references scattered through the docs. ## The three config files (all Tier 1 — frozen, `@tier-1-approvers` owned) | File | Role | |---|---| | `coderabbit.yaml` | Main config — review behaviour, path-specific instructions, tool toggles, merge gates | | `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` | Custom accessibility lint rules CodeRabbit runs via its `ast-grep` tool | | `semgrep.yml` | Custom security rules CodeRabbit runs via its `semgrep` tool | All three route to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` in `CODEOWNERS`, are listed in `frozenFiles.md`'s Governance section, and appear explicitly in the `tier1-guard` job's file list in `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml` — so touching CodeRabbit's config is exactly as gated as touching `AGENTS.md` itself. ## `coderabbit.yaml` — the main config - **`language: en-US`**, `profile: "assertive"` (pushes back harder), `request_changes_workflow: true` (can formally request changes, not just comment), `poem: false`. - **`path_instructions`** is the big one — per-path review criteria CodeRabbit applies automatically on every PR: - A repo-wide `overrides/**` block encodes 12 numbered checks: TS-only in overrides, SSR safety (`typeof window !== 'undefined'` guards), React Query cache invalidation on basket/customer/order mutations, Chakra token usage, `react-intl` for all copy, multi-region safety (no hardcoded currency/locale), Einstein/DataCloud event firing, WCAG 2.2 AA, performance (SSR blocking ops, unasync'd third-party scripts, full-res images), no console logs/PII, heightened scrutiny when a PR looks Claude-Code-generated, and Conventional Commits enforcement. - Then increasingly specific overrides for known-dangerous paths: `theme/foundation/**` (flag old/new hex values explicitly), each Tier 1 hook individually (`use-current-basket.ts` gets "grep every consumer before approving", `use-current-customer.ts`, `use-navigation.ts`, `use-multi-site.ts`), `config/**`, `mobify.config.js`, `.github/workflows/**`, `ssr.js`. - Tier 2 paths get their own instructions too: `header/**`, `routes.tsx`, `product-tile/**`, `display-price/**`. - Squad-specific business logic: `pages/checkout/**` (payment logging, 3DS flow, BOPIS toggle), `pages/product-detail/**` (variant resolution, Einstein ATC event, SSR prefetch, schema.org markup), `pages/product-list/**` (URL-based refinement/pagination for SEO). - Even `e2e/features/**` gets instructions — checks for the Jira tag, area tag, `@p0` correctness, no technical detail in Gherkin steps, file length, baseline/DELTA conventions. - **`tools`**: `eslint`, `gitleaks` (secret detection), `osvScanner` (dependency CVEs), `reactDoctor` (React-specific scanner), and the two custom ones: - `ast-grep` → points at `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules` (rules) and its `utils/` subfolder (shared fragments) - `semgrep` → points at root `semgrep.yml` - **`auto_review`**: reviews every push (not just PR-open), skips drafts, ignores `chore(deps)`/dependabot titles. - **`pre_merge_checks`** — the actual **merge-blocking** gates (this only works because `request_changes_workflow: true` is set above): - `title` (error) — Conventional Commits format - `description` (error) - `issue_assessment` (warning, not error yet — the Jira Forge app isn't installed in Atlassian yet, so there's nothing to assess against) - a `docstring-convention-compliance` custom check (error) — fails only for shared components (≥2 callers), exported hooks, or non-obvious utilities missing JSDoc. The blunt repo-wide `docstrings` gate is deliberately `mode: "off"` because it can't be path-scoped the way this custom check can. - **`finishing_touches.docstrings`**: on-demand JSDoc generation via a PR checkbox or `@coderabbitai` comment command. - **`chat.auto_reply`**: developers can ask CodeRabbit questions directly in PR comments. - **`knowledge_base.code_guidelines`**: this is what makes CodeRabbit actually *read* your rule files as review criteria — the config comment explains CodeRabbit reads literal file content and does **not** follow markdown links, so `AGENTS.md` linking to `.claude/rules/*.md` isn't enough on its own. Each rule file is wired in with an explicit `applyTo` glob: `conventions.md`/`typescript.md`/`css.md` → `overrides/**`, `components.md` → components/pages/hooks specifically, `testing.md` → `overrides/**` + `e2e/**`, `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md` → `**`. - **`knowledge_base.jira`**: scoped to project key `SFCC`, but flagged as inert until the Jira Forge app is installed — for now, Jira links have to be pasted into the PR description manually. - A header comment documents a real fix: an earlier version had a top-level `custom_instructions:` key and `version: "2"` that don't exist in the actual schema — silently doing nothing. The 12 rules were migrated into the `overrides/**` `path_instructions` entry so they'd actually take effect. ## `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` — 4 files, all accessibility - `img-missing-alt.yml` — flags any `` without `alt` - `icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml` — flags any `IconButton` without `aria-label` - `clickable-non-interactive-element.yml` — flags `div`/`span`/`Box`/`Flex`/`Stack`/etc. with `onClick` but no `role` - `utils/jsx-element.yml` — shared `jsxElement` matcher (opening or self-closing) the other three all reuse `components.md` calls these out directly: "mechanically enforced... get these right at authoring time." Contrast with `css.md`, which explicitly notes hardcoded hex/px values are **not yet** covered by an ast-grep rule — flagged as a good future candidate if it keeps slipping through review. ## `semgrep.yml` — 2 rules, both security - `payment-credential-logged` (taint mode) — traces variables named like `cardNumber`/`cvv`/`pin`/`pan` into `console.*` or `Sentry.*` sinks. Directly enforces the payment-credential rule in `conventions.md`. - `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` — flags `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: X}}` unless `X` is an obvious `*.sanitize(...)` call. ## How it relates to the GitHub Actions side `protected-file-guard.yml` is a *separate*, non-AI workflow that runs alongside CodeRabbit — it does the Tier 1/Tier 2/cross-squad file-list warnings via `tj-actions/changed-files`. Its `tier1-guard` job is explicitly informational, not a required check (a documented Feb-2025 GitHub platform change made a self-updating required check impossible — full explanation is in the job's comments and in `AGENTS.md`'s Tier 1 Approval section). CodeRabbit's `pre_merge_checks`, by contrast, **do** actually block merge — title/description/docstring gates are real gates, not just warnings. ## Where it surfaces in day-to-day docs `pr-checklist` skill has a dedicated "CodeRabbit pre-merge gates" checklist section (title format, Jira link, JSDoc on shared components/hooks) that mirrors the config directly. ## One small thing worth double-checking The file is `coderabbit.yaml` (no leading dot) everywhere it's referenced — `CODEOWNERS`, `frozenFiles.md`, `protected-file-guard.yml` all agree. But the file's own header comment says `# .coderabbit.yaml — Zimmermann PWA Kit` (with a dot), which doesn't match its actual name on disk. Minor internal inconsistency, probably just a stale comment — not something to fix unless you're touching that file for another reason (and if you are, it's Tier 1).

content.text:
Picture CodeRabbit as a **robot reviewer** who reads every code change before a human teammate does.

**Its instruction manual** (`coderabbit.yaml`) tells the robot: "in this part of the house, watch for this; in that part, watch for that." Checkout gets extra-strict instructions (it's where the money happens), the design-token files get "flag any colour change," and so on.

**It always carries two checklists in its pocket:**
- A **"can everyone use this?" checklist** (`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`) — does every picture have a caption (`alt`)? Does every icon-only button have a name tag (`aria-label`)? Is every clickable thing actually reachable by keyboard?
- A **"don't leave secrets lying around" checklist** (`semgrep.yml`) — did anyone write a credit card number somewhere it could leak into a log? Did anyone paste in a stranger's HTML without washing it first?

**Most of its comments are just friendly sticky notes** — but a few are "the door literally won't open" rules: wrong-shaped commit title, missing PR description, missing doc-comment on shared code. Those actually block the merge until fixed.

**And the instruction manual itself is locked in a glass case.** Nobody can quietly make the robot less strict — changing any of its three files needs the same big sign-off as changing the project's master rulebook.

content.text: ## The 30-second mental model Forget "AI" for a second. CodeRabbit is a reviewer that sits on every PR alongside your human reviewers. It reads the diff, reads *your* rulebook (AGENTS.md + the `.claude/rules/` files), and reacts — comments, pushes back, or in a few specific cases, physically won't let the PR merge until something's fixed. The reason it exists in this repo specifically: you've built a fairly elaborate constitution (frozen files, protected files, squad ownership, 15 hard rules) — but a human reviewer at 4pm on a Friday will forget to check all of that, every time, on every PR. CodeRabbit is the thing that makes the rulebook *actually get enforced* consistently, before a human even opens the diff. ## Building it up, piece by piece **Piece 1 — it's read your handbook.** Somewhere in `coderabbit.yaml` there's a section (`knowledge_base.code_guidelines`) that just says "here are the files that count as review criteria" — `AGENTS.md`, `conventions.md`, `css.md`, `components.md`, `frozenFiles.md`, etc. Worth knowing: CodeRabbit only reads the literal content of files you list — it doesn't click through markdown links. So `AGENTS.md` saying "see conventions.md" doesn't automatically pull `conventions.md` in; each file has to be listed explicitly, with a note on *which paths* it applies to. That's the mundane reason this section exists at all — it's not optional plumbing, it's the only reason CodeRabbit knows about any of your rules in the first place. **Piece 2 — it's got per-file playbooks, not just general vibes.** The bulk of `coderabbit.yaml` (the `path_instructions` block) is CodeRabbit being told, in plain English, "when you see a diff touching *this* file, here's specifically what to look for." Same idea as briefing a contractor: "if you're reviewing the basket hook, go check every place that imports it before you approve." The instructions get more specific as the file gets more dangerous — a broad instruction for anything under `overrides/**`, then much sharper, named instructions for `use-current-basket.ts`, `ssr.js`, `theme/foundation/`, checkout pages, etc. This is the same tiering logic as `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md` — just taught to the reviewer instead of enforced by GitHub permissions. **Piece 3 — two "dumb but reliable" specialists bolted on.** Alongside the AI judgement layer, CodeRabbit runs two pattern-matching tools that aren't AI at all — they're closer to a very targeted `grep` with syntax awareness: - **ast-grep** (`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`) — three rules, all accessibility: missing `alt` on an ``, missing `aria-label` on an `IconButton`, a clickable `div`/`Box`/`Stack` with no `role`. These aren't "the AI thinks this might be a problem" — they're mechanical, 100%-reliable-for-that-one-pattern checks. - **semgrep** (`semgrep.yml`) — two rules, both security: a payment-credential variable (`cardNumber`/`cvv`/`pin`) flowing into `console.*`/`Sentry.*`, and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` used without an obvious `.sanitize()` call. The reason both exist *separately* from the AI review: judgement-based review can miss things or be inconsistent; a narrow mechanical rule for a well-understood, high-cost mistake (leaked card numbers, XSS) never will. You trade flexibility for certainty on exactly the handful of mistakes you can't afford to have slip through. **Piece 4 — comments vs. locked doors.** Most of what CodeRabbit does is advisory — like a colleague leaving review comments you can push back on. But a small, explicit set of checks (`pre_merge_checks` in the config) are actual gates: PR title has to match Conventional Commits format, a description has to exist, and — this one's clever — any shared component or exported hook that's missing JSDoc fails a custom check. That last one only fails for things that actually matter (≥2 callers, or an exported hook), specifically because a blunt "every function needs a docstring" rule would've been both annoying and wrong for one-off leaf components. That distinction — advisory vs. blocking — is the single most important thing to internalize: most of the config is "help the reviewer," a small deliberate slice is "physically block the merge." **Piece 5 — the reviewer's rulebook is itself locked.** `coderabbit.yaml`, `.coderabbit/`, and `semgrep.yml` are all Tier 1 — same protection level as `AGENTS.md` itself. Makes sense once you see it as a system: if anyone could quietly edit the reviewer's instructions, every other protection in the repo becomes theater. So changing what CodeRabbit checks requires the same sign-off as changing the constitution it's enforcing. ## Now with the actual names attached | Plain-language concept | What it's actually called | |---|---| | "Read the handbook" | `knowledge_base.code_guidelines` | | "Per-file playbooks" | `path_instructions` | | "Accessibility pattern-matcher" | `tools.ast-grep`, rules in `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` | | "Security pattern-matcher" | `tools.semgrep`, rules in `semgrep.yml` | | "Locked doors" | `pre_merge_checks` (requires `request_changes_workflow: true` to have teeth) | | "Just comments" | everything else under `reviews:` | | Other built-in scanners | `tools.eslint`, `tools.gitleaks` (secrets), `tools.osvScanner` (dependency CVEs), `tools.reactDoctor` (React-specific) | One thing genuinely worth internalizing as FED lead: this is a *separate* system from the GitHub Actions `protected-file-guard.yml` workflow. That workflow does file-list-based tier warnings (dumb, reliable, GitHub-native). CodeRabbit does content-based judgement plus the two mechanical scanners. They run in parallel and cover different failure modes — one can't substitute for the other.

#!/bin/bash
# Pre-commit hook:
#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
#   2. Warn when staged components in components/ or ui/ have a paired
#      *ContentfulDefinition.ts that is not also staged.
#
# Install (run both — the commit-msg hook is a sibling that enforces conventional commits):
#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Registry regeneration — keeps .claude/registry/ in sync with
#    overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/ and routes.tsx/jsx.
#    Individually checked per location; skipped entirely (no node invocation
#    at all) when the commit doesn't touch any of them — e.g. a commit that
#    only touches config/ or tooling files. Stages any updated registry
#    files automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
  git add .claude/registry/
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null
    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
#     automatically. Placed before the Contentful check's early exit (below)
#     so it always runs regardless of whether component files are staged.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'

  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1d. .env.sample secret guard — BLOCKS the commit if a var whose name looks
#     like a secret (TOKEN/SECRET/KEY/PASSWORD/CREDENTIAL) has a non-empty
#     value staged in .env.sample. Real values belong only in .env (gitignored)
#     — see AGENTS.md > Rules > Environment variables. Checks the staged
#     (index) content, not the working tree, and runs before the Contentful
#     check's early exit below so it always executes.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then

    | grep -E '^[A-Z0-9_]*(TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL)[A-Z0-9_]*=.+$' \
    || true)

    echo ""
    echo "$leaked_vars" | sed -E 's/=.*/=<redacted>/' | sed 's/^/       /'
    echo ""

    echo "  PASSWORD/CREDENTIAL variables (see AGENTS.md > Rules > Environment variables)."
    echo "  Move the real value(s) to your local .env (gitignored) and blank them here."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Contentful definition drift check
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Staged .jsx/.tsx files scoped to components/ or ui/ directories only

  | grep -E '(components|ui)/.*\.(jsx|tsx)$' \
  | grep -v 'ContentfulDefinition' \
  || true)

  base=$(basename "$file")

  def_file="${dir}/${base}ContentfulDefinition.ts"

  [[ ! -f "$def_file" ]] && continue

  # Warn if the definition is not also staged alongside the component
  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF "$def_file"; then

  echo ""
  echo "  $WARNINGS component(s) may have stale Contentful definitions."
  echo "  Run /contentful-drift-check to review, then stage any updated definition files."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derived configuration file guard
#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

blocked_files=()

# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  # Only check files in derived locations
  case "$file" in
    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac

  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue

  # Extract the first source path from the synced-from comment
  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2] — ... -->
  # or:     <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md — ... -->
  synced_from=$(echo "$synced_line" \
    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//' \
    | sed 's/,.*//' \
    | tr -d ' ')

  [[ -z "$synced_from" ]] && continue

  # If the source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
  # update — the developer edited the .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
  # Skip it.
  if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF "$synced_from"; then
    continue
  fi

  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
  blocked_files+=("$file")

done <<< "$modified_staged"

if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
  echo ""
  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
    echo "       $bf"
  done
  echo ""
  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
  echo ""
  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
  echo ""
  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  secret_violations=()

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a JWT
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
      continue
    fi

  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)

  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
    echo ""
    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
      echo "    $v"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
    echo ""
    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

content.text:
Quick direct answers first, since you asked plainly: **it lives on GitHub, not in an Actions workflow and not as a VS Code extension.** I checked — `.vscode/extensions.json` only recommends Prettier and ESLint; nothing in this repo configures a CodeRabbit IDE extension. And `.github/workflows/` has no `coderabbit.yml` — the only workflow anywhere near this territory is `protected-file-guard.yml`, which is a completely separate system (more on that below). Now the mental model for how it actually sits in the day-to-day flow.

## The story of one PR, told in order

**1. You commit locally — CodeRabbit isn't there yet.**
Your `pre-commit` hook runs (registry regen, `.env.sample` secret scan, the "don't hand-edit derived AI config files" guard). None of that is CodeRabbit — it's pure local git hygiene, running entirely on your machine before anything touches GitHub.

**2. You push and open a PR against `develop`.**
This is the moment CodeRabbit enters the story. It's not something you invoke — it's a **GitHub App**, already installed on the org, sitting there listening for PR events the same way a Slack bot sits in a channel listening for messages. The instant the PR opens (and again on every subsequent push, because `auto_incremental_review: true`), it wakes up on its own, pulls the diff, reads `coderabbit.yaml`, and starts working. You don't run a command, don't click a button — it just shows up.

**3. It posts its review, same PR thread everyone already lives in.**
A summary comment (what changed, at a glance) plus inline comments on specific lines, the same visual place a human reviewer's comments would appear. Nothing separate to check, no second dashboard — it's in the PR conversation.

**4. Meanwhile, a totally different system is also running — easy to conflate, worth keeping separate in your head.**
`qa.yml` (Vitest/Storybook), `protected-file-guard.yml` (the tier/squad file warnings), `digital-sit.yml` on release branches — these are GitHub **Actions**, triggered by the same PR event but running as jobs *in this repo's own CI*, nothing to do with the CodeRabbit App. Actions = your repo's own scripted checks. CodeRabbit App = an external service GitHub is forwarding PR events to. Two different mechanisms, coincidentally both reacting to the same PR-opened moment.

**5. You can talk back to it, right there in the thread.**
`chat.auto_reply: true` means you can `@coderabbitai` in a PR comment — ask it why it flagged something, or ask it a question about the diff — and it replies conversationally. There's also a checkbox/command path (`finishing_touches`) to have it auto-generate missing JSDoc on demand rather than you writing it.

**6. Before merge, two independent gates have to clear — neither is "a human remembering to check."**
- CodeRabbit's own `pre_merge_checks` (PR title format, description present, the JSDoc-on-shared-stuff check) — these are configured in `error` mode with `request_changes_workflow: true`, which is what gives CodeRabbit's review actual teeth instead of just being a comment.
- Completely separately: **CODEOWNERS + GitHub's native branch protection** — if the PR touches a Tier 1/Tier 2 path, GitHub itself won't let the merge button light up without the required reviewer, regardless of what CodeRabbit says. This one has nothing to do with CodeRabbit at all — it's GitHub's own permission system.

## Attaching the jargon to the story

| Moment in the story | What it's called |
|---|---|
| "It just shows up on PR open/push" | GitHub App install + `auto_review.enabled` / `auto_incremental_review` |
| "Posts summary + inline comments" | the default `reviews:` behaviour |
| "Talk back to it" | `chat.auto_reply` |
| "On-demand JSDoc" | `finishing_touches.docstrings` |
| "Actually blocks the merge button" | `pre_merge_checks` (title/description/docstring-convention-compliance), only load-bearing because `request_changes_workflow: true` |
| "GitHub's own separate permission gate" | CODEOWNERS + branch protection (nothing to do with CodeRabbit config at all) |

One honest caveat, worth you specifically checking since you're the lead: whether CodeRabbit's `pre_merge_checks` status is actually wired up as a **required check** in the repo's branch protection rules is a GitHub web-UI setting, not something living in any file I can read from the repo. The config *asks* for merge-blocking behaviour, but whether GitHub's branch protection is actually configured to honor that as a hard block (vs. just a visible-but-overridable status) is worth confirming directly in GitHub → Settings → Branches for `develop`/`release/**`.

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review

8	Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com, a luxury Australian fashion brand. Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly. See [.docs/architecture.md](.docs/architecture.md) for stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths.
9	
10	Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).
11	
12	## Branch Rules
13	
14	**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.
15	
16	| Branch                    | Branched from          | Merges to                                                                       | Allowed?      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
17	| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
18	| `feature/*`               | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Primary working context for new work                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
19	| `fix/*`                   | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene                                                                                                                                                                                |

Sync complete — both `develop` and `feature/your-ticket-onboarding-setup` are at `4c2e389`, working tree clean. This was a much bigger pull: 3 merged PRs, 14 commits. Here's what actually matters out of it.

## The one that actually changes scope: US site topology (REG-005) flipped

`projectState.md` shows this wasn't cosmetic — it's a genuine decision reversal:
- **Before:** one US storefront handling both domestic (SFCC) and international (Global-e) checkout, branched by shipping address — 7 SFCC sites total.
- **Now (2026-07-10):** US splits into **two separate SFCC sites** — US domestic (`/us/`) and US international (`/en-ca/`, new site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl`, pending BM confirmation) — **8 SFCC sites** total.

This is echoed consistently in `testing.md`'s multi-region fixtures section too. Worth internalizing before you scope any multi-site or regional routing work — the "single US site, branch by address" model you might still have in your head is now stale.

## PR #23 — Contentful space bootstrap automation

New scripts (`scripts/contentful/setup/`: `bootstrapSpace.mjs`, `getConfig.mjs`, `runMigrations.mjs`, `promoteAlias.mjs`, `detectDrift.mjs`) plus matching `npm run setup:contentful` / `migrate:contentful` / `promote:alias` / `detect:drift` scripts, a new migration file, and `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts`. New devDependency: `contentful-cli`.

**Action needed:** `package-lock.json` changed by ~10,900 lines because of that new dependency — your local `node_modules` is now out of sync until you run `npm install`. Want me to run it?

## Your local `.env` is now stale — worth checking before you next run the app

`.env.sample` picked up real changes that your gitignored local `.env` won't have automatically:
- **`CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` changed** (`qxem2w4qko22` → `u9kb6gp6slxu`) — your local `.env` is likely still pointing at the old space.
- **New vars with no local counterpart yet:** `INSIDE_CHAT_SITE_TOKEN` (a prior open question — "does the PWA even need this?" — got resolved to yes, direct head-tag include, not via GTM), `MEASMERIZE_BRAND_CODE`, `OPTIMIZELY_PROJECT_ID` (now confirmed: `4599769641779200`), `GTM_CONTAINER_ID` (now confirmed: `GTM-M8PJ5D`), plus a whole new BrowserStack-local-testing block (`BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME`/`ACCESS_KEY`, `RETAIL_APP_HOME`, `PWA_E2E_USER_*`, fixture SKUs) for the new `npm run test:story` command.

Worth diffing your real `.env` against `.env.sample` before your next `npm start`.

## CI/testing rewrite (PR #25)

`qa.yml` + `testing.md` picked up two real workflow changes:
- **Change-scoped E2E** — `develop`-targeted PRs now only run the Playwright specs relevant to the changed-file area (falls back to full suite if anything falls outside a claimed area).
- **BrowserStack story-scoping** — `e2e-browserstack` now scopes to whatever `SFCC-NNN` Jira key it detects in the PR title/body/branch name; no key found means the job doesn't run at all (deliberate, not a gap). `npm run test:story` (new) is the local pre-push equivalent of this.

## Everything else, briefly

- **`AGENTS.md`** changed 65 lines but it's almost entirely markdown reformatting (table alignment, `*em*` → `_em_`). The one real addition: a new pointer to `.docs/integration/` docs for "how a specific integration works technically" (distinct from PRDs, which stay the source of truth for *requirements*).
- **`.docs/temp/integration/*` got promoted** to permanent `.docs/integration/` (out of the temp/draft folder), plus a new `14-inside-chat.md` and an `index.md`. `.docs/architecture.md` was also rewritten substantially (203 lines) — worth a fresh read given it's your core stack-overview doc.
- **`tsconfig.json`** — dropped a deprecated `baseUrl`, reformatted to 2-space indent. Tier 1, already merged, nothing for you to do.
- Remote housekeeping: `feature/docsCleanup` (the branch I flagged as new last sync) merged via PR #21 and its remote branch is now deleted. A new remote branch `fix/e2e-ci-timeout` appeared — not yours as far as I can tell, nothing to act on.
